current_episode.title: 112: How We Moved from Ireland and Built a Life for Our Family on The Costa del Sol [Our Story 10 Years On]

guest.bio_context: Warner moved from Ireland to the Costa del Sol in 2016 with his wife Sandra and two young children, Oliver and Abigail. He initially worked with another real estate firm for one year before launching WL Costa Properties in 2017. He built the business solo while his wife worked in the corporate sector, eventually growing it into a successful operation with podcast and online resources after seven years of focus on property sales and client relationships.

pending_qa.q: How can relocating professionals secure career-equivalent employment in a new country without prior language fluency?
pending_qa.r: Research companies with international footprints that are based in your target location, attack the job hunt strategically as a serious project, and believe in your skill set regardless of language barriers. In 2016, Malaga was gaining traction as a low-cost labor solution for international companies with nearshoring opportunities and tech hub growth. The speaker secured three job offers by targeting these internationally-focused companies, eventually staying with one for eight and a half years and reaching C-level director position without initial Spanish fluency.

pending_qa.q: What financial planning framework should families establish before relocating internationally?
pending_qa.r: Families must determine their monthly breakeven point—the minimum income needed to survive each month—and ensure that figure comes in consistently, just as they would budget in any other country. Without a clear financial plan and baseline number, savings will dwindle very fast. The speaker and his wife established this baseline early and made sure at least one person had stable, contracted permanent employment in the social security system.

pending_qa.q: Should families enroll young children in local language schools or international schools when relocating to a non-English speaking country?
pending_qa.r: Primary Spanish education is excellent, and children will integrate far more quickly into local Spanish schools than international schools. Oliver was four when moved and was the only non-Spanish speaking child in his class with a Spanish-speaking teacher who spoke no English; within one year he became fluent. The teacher, Rosario, was correct in her prediction, and having children in Spanish schools accelerates family integration because parents meet local people and are invited to speak Spanish.

pending_qa.q: How do young children develop resilience and social skills when immersed in a completely foreign language education system?
pending_qa.r: Children are more resilient than parents give them credit for. Oliver, who was thrown into Spanish primary school without prior primary school experience or Spanish language skills, developed exceptional social skills and curiosity about people. He did not have one best friend but became a social butterfly across multiple friend groups, suggesting that the challenge of adapting to a foreign educational system directly contributed to his ability to interact across diverse social contexts.

pending_qa.q: What approach to language learning do expatriate women commonly struggle with compared to men in international relocations?
pending_qa.r: Women tend to become perfectionist and get in their own head about language learning, whereas men naturally have more confidence and do not care as much about mistakes. The speaker's wife avoided kids' birthday parties and school meetings out of fear of making language errors, lost confidence, and held herself back for years. Men do not fall into this trap as readily and will speak without worrying about quality or perfection.

pending_qa.q: What triggered the business partnership transition from solo operation to joint family venture in a real estate firm?
pending_qa.r: After seven years of Warner building WL Costa Properties solo while his wife worked in corporate, something had to give. By the time their son turned 13, Warner's wife wanted to step back from corporate travel across Northern Europe and be more available to the family. She transitioned to part-time consulting for her previous company (25 hours per week for nearly a year), upskilled in online marketing and digital strategy, and then suggested to Warner that he was missing opportunities in reaching people, which led to the launch of the podcast and online resources.

pending_qa.q: How does spousal role-switching and division of labor support dual-career ambitions in family relocation?
pending_qa.r: One partner cannot have a big career in one place while the other pursues an equally demanding career—something has to give. The family's approach was to alternate focus: Sandra was breadwinner initially while Warner settled the kids for three months, then Warner built his real estate business while Sandra worked corporate, and finally Sandra stepped back to support Warner's business growth while maintaining part-time consulting. This teamwork approach allowed them to build a serious life rather than trying to do everything at once.
